title: AST Context Efficiency Benchmark (Graphify/R2R vs Grep)
refactoring_task: Refactor session token propagation across application and infrastructure modules

ast_subgraph.retrieval_method: 2-hop neighborhood extraction from Graphify AST graph (graph.json) via R2R

protocol_checklist.intent: Quantify context efficiency gains and attention degradation elimination using semantic AST graphs.
protocol_checklist.configuration: Repository with 120 files (>45,000 LoC Rust/Python). Task: refactor session token propagation. Baseline: keyword grep dumping matching files. Graph method: 2-hop neighborhood extraction from Graphify AST graph (graph.json) via R2R.
protocol_checklist.reality: AST graph cut prompt token volume from 38,400 to 3,150 tokens (91.8% token reduction) and retrieval latency from 3.8s to 420ms. First-pass pass rate reached 94% with graph vs. 62% with naive grep.
protocol_checklist.lessons: Precomputing AST graph in CI (graphify update) amortizes instantly across agent iterations, eliminating context bloat and 'lost-in-the-middle' hallucinations.
protocol_checklist.industrial_transfer: In legacy industrial software with millions of LoC (C++/C#/Rust), targeted AST subgraphs are the only cost-effective and accurate way to guide automated refactoring.
